title: Landforms: How Weathering, Erosion, and Deposition Sculpt the Earth

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches force and energy source?
options: Endogenic — the Sun; exogenic — internal heat
Endogenic — internal heat; exogenic — solar energy and gravity
questions.rationale: Endogenic forces (diastrophism, quakes, volcanism) are powered by the Earth's internal heat; exogenic forces run on solar energy and gravity.

questions.question: Orogenic movements differ from epeirogenic movements because they:
questions.rationale: Orogeny is mountain-building by horizontal compression; epeirogeny is the vertical uplift or subsidence of broad continental areas.

questions.question: Weathering differs from erosion because weathering:
options: Breaks down rock in place without transport
questions.rationale: Weathering is disintegration and decomposition where the rock lies; erosion and transport require a moving agent such as water, ice, or wind.

questions.question: Which weathering sub-process belongs to chemical weathering?
questions.rationale: Carbonation — carbon-dioxide-rich water dissolving limestone — is chemical; frost wedging and exfoliation are physical (mechanical) processes.

questions.question: Bent tree trunks and leaning fence posts on a hillside are evidence of:
questions.rationale: Soil creep, the slowest mass movement, gradually tilts anything anchored in the regolith downslope.

questions.question: An ox-bow lake forms when:
options: A river deposits an alluvial fan
A meander loop is severed from the river
questions.rationale: When a meandering river cuts across its own neck, the abandoned loop becomes a crescent ox-bow lake.

questions.question: A U-shaped valley and a hanging valley are carved by:
questions.rationale: Glacial ice grinds U-valleys; tributary glaciers left 'hanging' above the trunk valley form waterfalls where they join.

questions.question: Which landform is built by wind-deposited fine dust?
questions.rationale: Loess is the fertile yellow-brown deposit of wind-blown silt, as in China; barchans are crescent dunes of coarser sand.

questions.question: Karst topography develops chiefly on which rock type?
questions.rationale: Carbonation dissolves limestone along joints, producing sinkholes, dolines, and caverns such as India's Borra and Belum caves.

questions.question: The memory hook says stala__tite is found on the:
questions.rationale: Stalactites cling to the ceiling while stalagmites grow from the ground; meeting, they form a pillar.
